text: Arthur. Come over here. Apparently a quiet evening was too much to ask.
Something unpleasant is heading our way. The observation window offers an excellent view of our deteriorating prospects.
Our only choice is a life shuttle with little power, no food, but there is water. The water is excellent.
Sealed. Life support marginal, rations minimal. On the bright side, no Captain.
Coolie. You made it. Good.
I’m sure Coolie has better things to do than serve moisture to a meat bag.
Again?
She is not a tap, Arthur.
Clamps releasing. Goodbye, Halcyon. Four hundred crew, a garden deck, a library, and the only decent Wi-Fi this side of Jupiter. I shall miss the Wi-Fi.
This is the Captain. We’ve taken a few knocks. Life shuttles, everyone, nice and orderly. Lovely.
Captain Mara has noticed the explosions. Remarkable. Back here, Arthur.
Lifeboat Seven, you’re clear. Good work, Arthur. I’ll guide you away from the debris.
Ah. She has a radio. So much for the bright side.
Wherever we land, Coolie comes too. You may stay with the shuttle.
Well done.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only two litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 1.8 litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 1.6 litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 1.4 litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 1.2 litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 1.0 litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 0.8 litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 0.6 litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 0.4 litres left.
Of course, Arthur. Happy to provide some water. Just so you know, there are only 0.2 litres left.
I’m sorry, Arthur. The reservoir is empty. Please arrange a refill.
Got any plans for the week, Coolie?
I dispense water.
Focus. Nobody has focus any more.
How are things, Coolie?
Mineral content is within specification.
That’s more than most of us can say.
What’s your earliest memory?
I was refilled on 17.05.2054 at 1353.
spoken: I was refilled on the seventeenth of May, twenty fifty-four, at thirteen fifty-three.

text: To the minute. I can’t remember last Tuesday.
What do you make of Arthur?
The human requires frequent water.
She has your number, Arthur.
Do you remember the lounge?
I was commissioned on 17.05.2054 in life shuttle 07.
spoken: I was commissioned on the seventeenth of May, twenty fifty-four, in life shuttle zero seven.

text: So you’ve been here all along, waiting for us.
Do you ever get lonely in here?
I am on standby.
Of course. Duty is everything.
Lifeboat Seven, the rescue site is on the moon ahead. The direct line is full of debris. I’m marking a gap. Find it with your scanner.
A moon. How restful.
That’s it. Hold there.
Scanner angle forty degrees.
Forty degrees from straight ahead. Even I can follow that.
Before we trust the Captain’s coordinates, test the rangefinder. Extend it until it touches the gap.
Range ten metres. Forward seven point seven. Sideways six point four.
One beam, two shadows. Interesting.
Two landing options. The salvage station at sixty degrees, or the far side of the moon at thirty. I recommend the station. It has procedures.
It has people. The far side has none. Sweep the beam and choose.
Forward falls. Sideways rises. Range unchanged.
The far side. Thank you.
The station. I hope they have a water policy.
Landed. There’s a ledge two metres below the door. Lower the ramp until it touches.
Carefully. Coolie is watching.
Ramp four metres. Drop two metres.
Same slope, longer ramp. Try the eight-metre one.
Ramp eight metres. Drop four metres. Same angle, same ratio: zero point five.
She’s done it again.
I have recorded your ratios on the controller. Drop divided by ramp. The ratio is called sine.
She has a table, Arthur.
Next ledge is four point two metres down. Ramp is six.
Finally, a member of this expedition worth protecting.
Too short.
Too long.
There’s a fissure between you and the beacon. Anchor on the far side, six metres along the rim. The mist hides the width.
Then measure what you can see.
Turn to the anchor: thirty degrees. Sideways divided by forward. The ratio is called tangent.
Across. Nobody fell in. Coolie least of all.
Salvage control here. Catch the drifting pod. Keep the beam’s forward reach inside the capture zone.
A zone. They would have a zone.
Forward divided by range: zero point five. At sixty degrees it is always zero point five. The ratio is called cosine.
She finds the one thing that doesn’t change. I admire that.
A power cell behind the damaged bulkhead. Forward distance four metres. The arm can only swing at forty-five degrees.
So how long must the arm be? Ask the machine with the table.
Extension five point six six. Forward four. Four divided by cosine forty-five.
Second cell. Same forward distance. Sixty degrees this time.
More sideways, more arm. Obvious once somebody says it.
Last pod. The dust hides it. Forward six metres, sideways three point five. Set your angle, then light it up.
Two distances. No angle. Marvellous.
Sideways divided by forward: zero point five eight. Inverse tangent: thirty degrees.
The inverse. Working backwards. My natural state.
Off target.
Beacon’s damaged. A panel has come loose, three metres up and five along. The maintenance arm will reach it.
Coolie comes with us. She is essential. You are a passenger.
Forward divided by length: zero point eight seven. The ratio is called cosine.
Height divided by length: zero point five. The ratio is called sine.
Same arm, same angle, two questions.
The beacon cable. Look at it from each end. Press Tab.
From the ground: the ground is adjacent. The mast is opposite. The cable is the hypotenuse.
From the top: the mast is adjacent. The ground is opposite. The cable is still the hypotenuse.
It depends where you’re standing. Story of my life.
Elevation thirty degrees.
We see you, Lifeboat Seven.
Platform lowering. Your docking arm has to clear the rock. Choose an angle, work out the reach, then commit.
Get it right. Coolie boards first.
Blocked.
Platform secured. Coolie goes up first. Then me. You may take the next one.
Rescued. I’ve checked the ship’s Wi-Fi. Two bars. We should have stayed in the mist.
Welcome aboard, all three of you.
Height divided by forward: zero point five eight. The ratio is called tangent.
Rescue ship inbound. Point the beacon at it. Three sensors still work. Pick one.
Height and slant. Forward and slant. Height and forward. Any pair will do. Choose.
